ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.11 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route segment; no account flag on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is a metered RydeTAXI trip Compass One → Kallang Wave Mall in which the GPS record shows one off-route segment, 23:03–23:14, driving 7.28 km where the optimal route covers 2.25 km and adding 5.04 km, drifting up to 2060 m off the optimal route, on a trip that ran 18.7 km against a 13.3 km optimal route (+40%) [F1][F3]. The driver's obligation is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and RD-1 sets no percentage or km threshold, so this measured deviation requires justification [RD-1].

The only candidate consent is F9: the driver asked at 22:59 whether he could "go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road" [F8] and the rider replied "Sure, no problem." at 23:00 [F9], before the segment began at 23:03 [F3]. That is a rider message sent in time, but it is a specific named-road authorisation, not a general route choice, so it covers driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road only [RD-5]. Nothing in the record ties the driven segment to that road: F3 carries only km and distance from the route, and the driver's own statement says he went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it "looked clearer" [F11]. Under RD-5, where the record places the segment on another road named by the driver himself, the agreement to the named road does not cover it — this is not the undetermined G13 situation, because the record does settle the correspondence against the agreed road [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip claim that the rider agreed is a claim only and cannot enlarge F9 (G11) [F11].

No RD-3 stop exemption applies: the segment contains no rider-named stop and the rider named no place at all — the reroute was the driver's proposal, not an errand of the rider's [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. No RD-4 exemption applies: the code-settled screen fails RD-4(a) — no traffic incident was recorded near the replaced stretch [F15] — and the only congestion record, the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway at band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 22:40 to 23:03 [F12], ends exactly when the off-route segment begins and band corroboration alone cannot exempt a segment [RD-4]. The segment is therefore unexempted.

On quantum, the trace's binding formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × this trip's per-km rate, the rate being the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km [RD-2]. The trace computes $7.11 for this segment; I compute $7.11 as follows. Reading F4's own figures — it bills 5.32 km at a stated $1.4102/km (which matches F7's distance fare $26.30 ÷ distance 18.65 km, itself 5.32 × 1.4102 = $7.50) — the trace's rate field is the stated $1.4102/km [F4][F7]. Applying that rate to the segment's added distance of 5.04 km from F3 [F3]: 5.04 km × $1.4102/km = $7.1074 ≈ $7.11. I therefore refund $7.11.

The metered waiting unit of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is chargeable under RD-3(c) and is not refunded; surge is 1.0× and there is no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 is not engaged [F5][F6][RD-3][FARE-1].

RD-6's account flag does not attach: F18 shows the driver's one upheld dispute is route: 0 / no-show: 0, so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and the repeated-breach condition is not met [F18][RD-6]; the trace likewise marks RD-6 ✗. The clean rider profile [F17] does not affect the outcome.

On the safety screen, I read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint: the chat is only a reroute request and an agreement [F8][F9], and the complaint and statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing meets SAFE-1 or SAFE-2, so no escalation is warranted [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS segment, the fare record and the complete timestamped two-message chat [F10] settle every element the ruling needs, so no gap exists.

rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected on quantum: the rider seeks $7.50 based on F4's billed excess distance of 5.32 km, but the trace's binding formula refunds only the unexempted segment's extra km at the fare rate, i.e. 5.04 km × $1.4102/km = $7.11, not the whole billed excess; F3 supplies the refundable extra km [F3][F4][RD-2].

The concession that the consent reaches only Upper Paya Lebar Road and is sent in time is correct, but the record does not leave the correspondence undetermined: F11 places the driven segment on Hougang Avenue 3, so RD-5 makes the segment count rather than sending the case to a human under G13 [F11][F3][RD-5].

F12 is a band-2 congestion record on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway ending at 23:03, exactly when the off-route segment begins [F3], and F15 records no incident near the replaced stretch, so RD-4(b) corroboration alone does not exempt the segment [F12][F15][RD-4].

The cap argument is accepted as to exposure but not as to the exact figure: the recoverable amount is the segment's extra km at the fare rate ($7.11), and the complaint that the fare far exceeded the estimate cannot be recovered beyond that on a metered trip [F4][F7][RD-2].

Rejected: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the one upheld dispute is route: 0, no-show: 0), so no flag_account attaches [F18][RD-6]; the rider advocate withdrew this in rebuttal.

The no-flag conclusion is accepted on the merits: F18 shows the driver's 1 upheld dispute is route: 0 / no-show: 0, so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and RD-6's repeated-breach condition is not met [F18][RD-6].

The safety reading is accepted: F8, F9 and F10 contain only a reroute request and agreement with no threat, intimidation or harassment, and no dangerous-driving or injury allegation appears in the record, so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged [F8][F9][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].
